To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of dormant cells reflects the initial capacity of cambium to accomplish division, the annual phloem increment was narrower, less variable and had lower and upper limits, and with increased cambial cell production, the share of xylem in total radial increment increased following curvilinear function.
the width of phloem increments is a reliable indicator of tree vitality and that the width of xylem increments and the number of dormant cells are less reliable indicators of tree vitality.
the structure and width (i.e., number and width) of dormant cambium, phloem and annual radial increment are useful indicators of tree vitality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of the anatomical structure and width of phloem, xylem and dormant cambium as indicators for tree vigor and vitality.
the potential use of anatomical variables to assess the vitality of trees in forest stands.
the potential of the structure of dormant and active cambium, as well as the width of xylem, phloem, and annual increments to be used as indicators of the vitality of oaken trees.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of dormant cells, the width of the phloem and the xylem increments and the ratio between them are all good indicators of tree vitality.

, although the width and structure and the relationships among the anatomical variables analyzed in this study may be used as indicators of tree vitality, they are not sufficient for a comprehensive assessment of vitality.
the structure of dormant and active cambium and the width of xylem increments can be used as indicators of tree vitality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of dormant cells is the most sensitive indicator, whereas the annual phloem width is the most stable indicator of tree vitality.
the width of the phloem increment is an important parameter for assessing tree vitality.
the number of dormant cells is a good indicator of the initial capacity of cambial activity, whereas the width of phloem increments is a good indicator for the vitality of trees.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the width of the phloem and the number of dormant cells can be used as indicators of tree vitality, whereas the width of the xyleem can be used as indicator of tree vitality only in combination with other indicators.
the structure of the dormant cambial cells is not a good indicator of the vitality of oaked.
the number of dormant cells and the width and the structure of phloem increments can be useful as indicators of tree vitality.
